name: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
aliases: Intestinal T-cell lymphoma associated with celiac disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of malignant T-cell infiltration in the intestinal epithelium with characteristic morphology
Expression of CD3+, CD7+, CD103+, and cytotoxic markers with loss of CD5 and CD8 in tumor cells
Association with refractory celiac disease or history of celiac disease
Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant T-cell infiltration with supportive immunophenotyping findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other intestinal lymphomas and correlation with clinical history of celiac disease.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Weight loss associated with intestinal lymphoma

imaging: CT scan showing thickened intestinal loops with ulcerations
other: Endoscopic biopsy revealing villous atrophy and lymphomatous infiltration
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytotoxic markers (TIA-1, granzyme B)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of overt lymphoma on biopsy
Presence of aberrant intraepithelial lymphocytes without mass lesions
Lack of association with celiac disease

redFlags: Rapid unexplained weight loss in celiac disease patient
Persistent or worsening malabsorption despite strict gluten-free diet
New onset abdominal mass or severe abdominal pain
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Cellier C, Delabesse E, Helmer C, et al. Refractory sprue, coeliac disease, and enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma. Lancet. 2000;356(9225):203-208.
Malamut G, Cellier C. Enteropathy-associated T cell lymphoma: improving treatment strategies. Curr Hematol Malig Rep. 2015;10(3):243-250.
